title: Coffee Production — East Africa Varieties and Management
content:
## Coffee (Coffea arabica / Coffea canephora) — East Africa

Coffee is a major export crop in Kenya, Ethiopia, Uganda, and Tanzania highlands.

### Recommended Varieties (Kenya — KALRO)

**Arabica (highland, >1500m):**
- **Ruiru 11** — resistant to CBD and leaf rust; widely planted
- **Batian** — high yield, CBD and rust resistant
- **SL28 / SL34** — premium cup quality; susceptible to CBD — use only with good fungicide program
- **K7** — drought tolerant; lower altitude tolerance

**Robusta (lowland, <1200m):**
- **Nganda conilon** — Uganda/Tanzania lowland zones

### Planting

- Spacing: 2.5m × 2.5m (1600 trees/ha) or 2m × 2m for high density
- Plant at onset of long rains; shade trees (Grevillea, Albizia) recommended in hot areas
- First harvest: year 2–3 (stumped), full yield year 4–5

### Fertilizer

- Apply NPK 17-17-17 at 200g per tree twice per year (long and short rains)
- Boron foliar spray at flowering improves cherry set

### Key Diseases

See also: Coffee Berry Disease (CBD), Coffee Leaf Rust entries in pest guides.

## Kahawa Afrika Mashariki

### Aina za KALRO Kenya

- **Ruiru 11** — inakabiliana na CBD na kutu ya majani
- **Batian** — mazao mengi, inakabiliana na magonjwa
- **SL28 / SL34** — ubora wa juu wa kikao; haitoshiwi na dawa za kuvu

### Upanzi

- Umbali: mita 2.5 × 2.5
- Panua mwanzo wa mvua za masika
- Mavuno ya kwanza: mwaka 2–3

title: Coffee Berry Disease (CBD) — Colletotrichum kahawae
content:
## Coffee Berry Disease (CBD) — Colletotrichum kahawae

CBD is the most destructive fungal disease of Arabica coffee in Kenya highlands. It is a **notifiable disease** — report severe outbreaks to the Coffee Research Institute (CRI) or local extension officer.

### Symptoms

- Young green berries (2–15 weeks after flowering) develop dark sunken lesions
- Berries turn black and mummify on the branch — they do NOT fall easily
- Berries may look normal externally until opened — interior is black and rotten
- In severe cases, entire cherry clusters are lost before ripening
- Also affects young stems and leaves in wet conditions

### Conditions Favoring CBD

- High altitude (>1600m), cool wet weather, frequent rain and cloud cover
- Peak infection: long rains (April–June) and short rains (October–December)

### Management

**Preventive (essential on susceptible varieties SL28, SL34):**
- Copper-based fungicides: Copper oxychloride (e.g. Kocide) 3–4 kg/ha every 21–28 days during rainy season
- Start spraying at first flower flush — do NOT wait for symptoms
- Systemic fungicides: Azoxystrobin (Amistar) or Pyraclostrobin (Comet) — rotate with copper to prevent resistance

**Cultural:**
- Plant resistant varieties: Ruiru 11, Batian
- Prune for airflow; remove mummified berries and destroy (burn, do not compost)
- Maintain shade at 30–40% — too dense shade increases humidity

**Harvest:**
- Pick only ripe red cherries; remove and destroy black mummified berries during harvest

### Distinguishing CBD from Other Coffee Problems

| Problem | Key feature |
|---------|-------------|
| CBD | Black mummified berries on tree, young green berries affected |
| Antestia bug | Multiple small punctures, "potato taste" defect in cup |
| Over-ripe | Cherry is fully red/black but not mummified |
| Drought stress | Cherry shrivels but does not turn black with fungal growth |
content_sw:
## Ugonjwa wa Coffee Berry Disease (CBD)

CBD ni ugonjwa wa kuvu unaoharibu zaidi kahawa ya Arabica milimani Kenya.

### Dalili

- Cheri za kijani zina vidonda vyeusi
- Cheri zinageuka nyeusi na kuoza kwenye mti kabla ya kuiva
- Ndani ya cheri ni nyeusi na imeoza

### Kudhibiti

- Dawa ya shaba (Kocide): kilo 3–4/hekta kila wiki 3–4 wakati wa mvua
- Panda aina zinazostahimili: Ruiru 11, Batian
- Ondoa cheri zilizokufa na uzichome

title: Coffee Leaf Rust — Hemileia vastatrix
content:
## Coffee Leaf Rust (CLR) — Hemileia vastatrix

CLR is a fungal disease causing orange powdery pustules on the underside of coffee leaves. It can defoliate trees and reduce yield 30–50%.

### Symptoms

- Yellow-orange spots on upper leaf surface
- Orange-brown powdery pustules on leaf underside (key ID feature)
- Premature leaf drop; exposed cherries sun-scald
- First appears on lower, inner canopy where humidity is highest

### Control

- Triazole fungicides: Propiconazole (Tilt), Hexaconazole — apply at first sign, repeat every 4 weeks in wet season
- Copper sprays as preventive on resistant varieties
- Plant resistant varieties: Ruiru 11, Batian (resistant to both CBD and CLR)
- Remove heavily infected fallen leaves from orchard floor
content_sw:
## Kutu ya Majani ya Kahawa (Coffee Leaf Rust)

Dalili: madoa ya manjano-kahawia juu ya jani; unga wa kahawia chini ya jani.

Tiba: dawa za kuvu (Propiconazole); panda aina zinazostahimili (Ruiru 11, Batian).
